interface.title: vizarr (standalone web app)
interface.stage_of_work: Looking at and checking images after they are taken or registered, before analysis
interface.what_it_is_for: Open a remote multiscale, multichannel OME-Zarr image from a URL in the browser, then turn channels on and off, recolor them, set contrast, step through Z, and pan or zoom. The README names viewing several pyramidal OME-Zarr images together, such as the outputs of image registration, as vizarr's main use; this run had a single-image store, so that use was not reached. This run covers only the standalone web app; the notebook Python API, the README's second main interface, was out of scope.

data.note: IDR example idr0062-blin-nuclearsegmentation/6001240.zarr, given in ?source=. It is a single image (image_0) with two channels, LaminB1 (blue by default) and Dapi (yellow), and 236 Z slices (labelled 0–235), opening at Z 118. It has no time axis. The full-resolution plane is small (about 270×275 px), so the pyramid has few levels. With no ?source the app shows only an empty black page with no message (screens/054.webp).

features.name: Per-channel display list with toggle, color and contrast
features.general: A list of signals, each with an on/off switch, a color, a two-ended display range slider and a settings menu; the overlay redraws as any of them changes
features.specific: vizarr channel rows: a circle toggle, a range slider colored to match the channel, and a ••• popover with selection, contrast limits (two number fields) and 7 color swatches
steps: Turn individual channels on or off with the circle toggle
Open ••• and pick a color swatch (cyan, yellow, magenta, red, green, blue or white)
Drag the range slider's lower and upper handles, or type exact min and max contrast limits
Typing a new maximum re-scales the slider's range to it

Note, seen only in the first run and not tried on replay: a minimum above the maximum was accepted without warning, turned the channel into a hard threshold, and couldn't be undone from the fields or the slider; only removing and re-adding the channel fixed it
serves_tasks: Show one signal on its own by hiding the others
Give each signal a color so the overlay reads clearly
Brighten dim signal by lowering the top of the display range
Remove background by raising the bottom of the display range

features.name: Channel row add, reassign and remove
features.general: Build the set of displayed channels: add a row for a chosen stored signal, point an existing row at a different signal, or delete a row
features.specific: 'channels: +' opens a selection dropdown (None / LaminB1 / Dapi) that adds a row; each row's ••• 'selection' dropdown re-points it; 'remove –' deletes it
steps: Click 'channels: +' and choose a channel name
A new row appears with default contrast (0–1500) in the next default color (blue on replay)
Change the row's selection to another channel index if needed
Remove an unwanted row with remove –

Note, seen only in the first run and not confirmed on replay: choosing Dapi from + added LaminB1 both times (replay chose LaminB1 only, so it could not check this), the new row drew from the starting Z (118) until Z was changed, and adding a row reset another row's contrast (replay saw no reset)
serves_tasks: Add a displayed channel, or take one away
Choose which stored signal a displayed channel shows

features.name: Dimension slider with exact index entry
features.general: Step through an extra image dimension (depth or time) with a slider, an exact-number field, or the arrow keys, and redraw all channels at that position
features.specific: 'Z: n/235' slider in the layer panel; its ••• opens an 'Index:' number field; arrow keys step by one once the thumb has focus
steps: Drag the Z slider to a rough depth
Open ••• and type an exact Index, then press Enter
Click the thumb and press ArrowRight or ArrowLeft to step one slice
Wait for the tiles to load (the label changes before the image does)

features.name: Multiscale pan and zoom canvas with view state in the URL
features.general: A tiled image viewer that loads finer levels of a pyramid as you zoom, and writes the current position and zoom into the page link so the view can be shared or reopened
features.specific: deck.gl/Viv canvas: wheel zooms, double-click zooms one step, drag pans; ?viewState={target,zoom} updates live and is read back on load
steps: Scroll the wheel over a region to zoom in toward the cursor
Double-click to zoom in one step
Drag to pan
Scroll down to zoom out to the whole field
Copy or reload the URL; target and zoom come back, but channel colors, contrast and Z go back to their defaults
serves_tasks: Zoom in to the finest detail and move around
Zoom out to see the whole field
Reopen a saved view position from a link

features.name: Layer card with visibility, opacity and collapse
features.general: A collapsible card for each image layer, with a show/hide eye and an opacity slider for the whole layer
features.specific: image_0 accordion header with an eye toggle and an opacity slider; clicking the header collapses the card to the header plus the opacity row
steps: Drag opacity to fade the layer
Click the eye to hide or show the layer (the icon gains a slash; the card stays open)
Click the header to collapse or expand the layer's controls
serves_tasks: Fade the whole image or hide it
Hide the controls to see the whole image

features.name: Open an image from a link
features.general: Open a remote image store by giving its address in the page link, with no upload or file dialog
features.specific: ?source=<OME-Zarr URL> in the page address; there is no input box on the page
steps: Put the store's address in the page link as ?source=<URL> and load the page
Wait about a second while the page is black, until the layer panel and image draw
The current view position is then added to the link as viewState
Note: with no ?source the page stays black with no message
serves_tasks: Open a remote image by putting its address in the page link

features.name: Hide-panel button
features.general: A button that hides the whole control panel so the image fills the window, and brings it back
features.specific: top-left – button hides the layer panel and turns into +; + shows it again
steps: Click – to hide the whole panel
Click + to bring it back
serves_tasks: Hide the controls to see the whole image

screens_never_reached: Time (T) slider: this dataset has no time axis, so only Z was offered

Several images viewed together (multi-layer view), which the README names as vizarr's main use for registered OME-Zarr images, and the plate or well grid for high-content screens (src/layers/grid-layer.ts): the example store holds one image, so only image_0 appeared. Feature not reached.

Segmentation label overlays: the code has a labels row with an on/off toggle and an opacity slider (src/components/LayerController/Labels.tsx, src/io.ts), but this dataset showed no labels. Feature not reached.
Any loading or error message for a missing or bad source: with no ?source the page is blank with no text (screens/054.webp)
